mainTopic: Gift incense is forbidden; the כהן גדול's daily חביתין: one full עשרון split in half, how it is prepared, and why it overrides שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that says incense (קטורת) may never be brought as a voluntary gift. Neither a ציבור nor a יחיד may bring it, and it may not be offered on either altar. רב פפא explains that the ברייתא uses a 'לא מיבעיא' style, and that the incense of the נשיאים was only a הוראת שעה. A new משנה then teaches that the כהן גדול brings one full עשרון of flour for his daily חביתין, splits it, and offers half in the morning and half in the afternoon. If he dies after the morning half, his replacement brings a fresh full עשרון, so two halves are offered and two are lost. A ברייתא learns all this from the word ״מַחֲצִיתָהּ״, and רב נחמן and רב אשי discuss why both leftover halves must be left overnight (עיבור צורה) before burning. The גמרא then records a dispute about whether the חביתין are baked before or after frying, based on readings of the word ״תֻּפִינֵי״. Finally it asks why preparing the חביתין overrides שבת. רב הונא, the school of רבי ישמעאל, and אביי each give a source, and אביי's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even the community may not bring gift incense
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא considers that a ציבור might be allowed to bring incense as a gift, since it already brings required incense. The plural word 'לא תעלו' rules this out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a community should be allowed to bring incense as a gift, since it brings a required incense offering just like it. That is why the verse says 'You (plural) shall not bring up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting a ברייתא. Here the ברייתא shows that even a ציבור may not bring incense as a voluntary gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is that whoever brings a required incense offering could also bring a voluntary one. The ציבור does bring required incense every day. But the verse uses a plural word, 'תעלו', and that plural includes the ציבור in the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to it; of the same kind
The verse teaches (to reject a possible thought)

phrases.english: But a community should be able to bring it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means incense as a voluntary gift. The ברייתא just finished saying an individual can't bring it.

phrases.english: since it brings an obligatory offering like it,
therefore the verse says: 'You shall not bring up.'
phrases.notes: שמות 30:9. The word is plural, so the ban covers the community too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא the גמרא was quoting just before this section, which is being set against an earlier source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier source that implied gift incense is sometimes allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This ברייתא bans gift incense even for the ציבור.

steps.title: Gift incense is not allowed on the outer altar either
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the idea that gift incense could go on the outer altar. The verse limits incense to exactly what was commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think they may not offer it on the inner altar but may offer it on the outer altar. That is why the verse says: 'The anointing oil and the incense of spices for the holy place, according to all that I commanded you they shall do.' You have only what is stated in this passage.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes one more loophole. Gift incense cannot be offered on the מזבח החיצון either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'ככל אשר צויתך יעשו' means incense must be done exactly as commanded and nothing more. It must be required, it must come from the ציבור, and it must go on the inner altar. This clashes with an earlier source that seemed to allow an individual's incense on the inner altar, or the ציבור's incense on the outer altar.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner (golden) altar, where incense is normally burned
The outer altar, where animal offerings are brought

keyTerms.term: אֵין לְךָ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁאָמוּר בָּעִנְיָן
keyTerms.meaning: You only have what the passage states; no extras

steps.confusionAlert: This is still the ברייתא talking. The clash with the earlier source is what רב פפא answers in the next step.

phrases.english: One might think they may not offer it on the inner altar,
but they may offer it on the outer altar?
Therefore the verse says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁאָמוּר בָּעִנְיָן.
phrases.english: you have only what is stated in the passage.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יַעֲלוּ עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, extending the ban to the outer altar.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier source implying that an individual's incense on the inner altar, or community incense on the outer altar, could be allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse limits incense to exactly what was commanded, so no gift incense on any altar.

steps.title: רב פפא explains the ברייתא with a 'goes without saying' style
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the ברייתא lists the obvious cases first, then adds 'even' the less obvious one. The incense of the נשיאים was a one-time ruling and sets no precedent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The ברייתא is speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say the community can't offer it on the outer altar, since we never find that. There is no need to say an individual can't offer it on the inner altar, since we never find that. But even an individual on the outer altar is not allowed, though we find it with the princes. That was a one-time ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the contradiction. He shows that the source which seemed to allow some gift incense was really building up to 'even this is forbidden'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases that have no precedent are obviously banned. The only real question is an individual's incense on the outer altar, because the נשיאים did bring incense. רב פפא says that was a הוראת שעה, a special ruling for that moment only, so it proves nothing for the future.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes without saying; a 'not only... but even' style
A temporary, one-time ruling, not a precedent

steps.whatToRemember: Gift incense is never allowed: not from a ציבור, not from a יחיד, and not on either altar. The נשיאים' incense was only a הוראת שעה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of הוראת שעה lets the גמרא explain away an unusual event in the תורה so it doesn't become a lasting rule.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is speaking in a 'no need to say' style,

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא צִיבּוּר עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן,
phrases.english: there is no need to say the community on the outer altar,
since we have not found it,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא יָחִיד עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי,
phrases.english: and there is no need to say an individual on the inner altar,
since we have not found it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ יָחִיד עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן,
phrases.english: but even an individual on the outer altar is forbidden,
though we found it with the princes:
phrases.notes: At the dedication of the משכן, each prince brought a spoon full of incense (במדבר 7).

phrases.english: that was a one-time ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised by the ברייתא in steps 1-2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the earlier source as a 'לא מיבעיא' list rather than a list of permitted cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier source seemed to allow some kinds of gift incense.
steps.terutzMaskana: All gift incense is banned. The source was only stressing that even the hardest case, an individual on the outer altar, is forbidden.

steps.title: New משנה: the כהן גדול's griddle-cakes come from one full tenth
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול does not bring his daily flour in two half portions. He brings one full עשרון, divides it, and offers half in the morning and half in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The griddle-cakes of the כהן גדול did not come in halves. Rather, he brings a full tenth of flour and divides it. He offers half in the morning and half in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: the חביתין offering of the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is about how the flour is brought, not how much is offered. Even though each offering is only half, the כהן גדול must start from one complete עשרון and split it.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily griddle-cake offering of the כהן גדול
A tenth of an איפה, a set measure of flour

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The griddle-cakes of the High Priest
did not come in halves,
phrases.notes: He means the flour wasn't brought from home as two separate half-measures.

phrases.english: rather he brings a full tenth and divides it,
he offers half in the morning
and half in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חֲבִיתֵּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל לֹא הָיוּ בָּאִין חֲצָאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the incense discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול brings one full עשרון for his חביתין, splits it, and offers half in the morning and half in the afternoon.

steps.title: When the כהן גדול dies after the morning half
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן גדול dies after offering the morning half, the new כהן גדול brings a fresh full עשרון, divides it, and offers half. Two halves end up offered and two halves are lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן גדול offered half in the morning and then died, and another was appointed in his place. The new one does not bring a half-עשרון from home, and he does not use the leftover half of the first כהן גדול. He brings a whole עשרון, divides it, offers half, and the other half is lost. So two halves are offered and two halves are lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the rule from the last step to a tricky case: the כהן גדול dies between the morning and afternoon offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the replacement could finish with the first כהן גדול's leftover half, or bring just a half from home. The משנה rejects both options. The afternoon half must come from a full עשרון that belongs to the person offering it, so the replacement starts over with a new whole עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: is lost (not offered, goes to waste)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the new כהן גדול 'finishes the job' with the old flour. The old כהן גדול's second half is simply lost, and the new one's second half is lost too.
steps.whatToRemember: Every half that is offered must be half of a complete עשרון belonging to the כהן גדול who offers it. That is why two halves get lost.

phrases.english: A priest who brings half in the morning,
phrases.notes: This means the כהן גדול and his daily flour offering from the last step.

phrases.english: and died, and they appointed another priest in his place –
he should not bring half a tenth from his house
nor use half of the tenth of the first one,
rather, he brings a whole tenth and divides it,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. Either way, the point is that he divides a whole tenth.

phrases.english: he offers half, and half is lost.
It turns out that two halves are offered,
and two halves are lost.
phrases.notes: One leftover half from each כהן גדול goes to waste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 4's rule (one full עשרון, divided in half) to the case where the כהן גדול dies midday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The replacement כהן גדול brings a new full עשרון and offers half of it. The leftover halves of both כהנים are lost.

steps.title: What we would have thought without the exact wording
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if the פסוק had only said 'a meal offering, half,' we would think he brings a separate half-עשרון from home each morning and each evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If the פסוק had said 'a meal offering, half,' I would have said that he brings half a tenth from his house in the morning and offers it, and brings half a tenth from his house in the evening and offers it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that looks for the source of the משנה's rule. This step only sets up the mistaken first idea, and the next step will correct it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא imagines a simpler wording of the פסוק. With that wording, two separate half-portions, each brought on its own, would seem good enough. This sets up why the actual words of the פסוק matter.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
I would have said (the mistaken first idea)

phrases.english: GEMARA
The Rabbis taught:
Had it said 'a meal offering, half,'
phrases.notes: This is an imagined, simpler version of ויקרא 6:13, without the word 'of it.'

phrases.english: I would have said

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא חֲצִי עִשָּׂרוֹן מִבֵּיתוֹ שַׁחֲרִית וּמַקְרִיב,
phrases.english: he brings half a tenth from his house in the morning and offers it,
and half a tenth from his house in the evening and offers it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's search for the פסוק behind the משנה's rule of one full עשרון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without the exact wording, two separate half-עשרון portions would seem acceptable.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches half of a complete עשרון
steps.stepSummary: The word 'מחציתה' ('half of it') shows that each half must come from one whole עשרון. He brings a whole עשרון, divides it, and offers half in the morning and half in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.' This means he offers half of a whole one. How does this work? He brings a whole tenth, divides it, and offers half in the morning and half in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא corrects the mistaken idea from step 6 by pointing to the exact words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending 'ָהּ' ('of it') points back to the whole עשרון mentioned earlier in the פסוק. So each half has to be a half of that one whole portion, not a separate half brought by itself. This is the source for the rule stated in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: half taken from a complete whole
how so? (how does this work in practice)

steps.whyThisMatters: This derivation is the basis for the משנה's surprising result in step 5, where halves are lost instead of being used.

phrases.english: The verse teaches
'half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:13

phrases.english: he offers half of a whole one,
How so?
He brings a whole tenth and divides it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַקְרִיב מֶחֱצָה בַּבֹּקֶר וּמֶחֱצָה בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם.
phrases.english: and offers half in the morning and half in the afternoon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 6's mistaken idea by pointing to the word 'מחציתה.'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each half offered must be half of one complete עשרון that was brought and divided.

steps.title: If the afternoon half becomes impure or is lost
steps.stepSummary: If the afternoon half becomes טמא or is lost, he cannot just bring a half-עשרון from home. The same פסוק requires a half of a complete עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the afternoon half became impure or was lost, you might think he could bring half a tenth from his house in the evening and offer it. The פסוק says 'half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening,' so he must bring half of a whole one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the same פסוק to a new case: the afternoon half is ruined after the morning half was already offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since only a half is missing, it seems logical to replace just a half. The ברייתא says no. Even a replacement must be half of a complete עשרון, so he brings a new whole עשרון and divides it.

keyTerms.meaning: one might think (introduces a mistaken idea)

steps.whatToRemember: Whether the כהן גדול dies or the afternoon flour is ruined, the rule stays the same: a fresh full עשרון, divided, with half offered.

phrases.english: If the afternoon half became impure,
or was lost,

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יָבִיא חֲצִי עִשָּׂרוֹן מִבֵּיתוֹ עַרְבִית וְיַקְרִיב?
phrases.english: one might think he should bring half a tenth from his house in the evening and offer it?
The verse teaches 'half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening' –
he brings half of a whole one.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִטְמָא מֶחֱצָה שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם, אוֹ שֶׁאָבַד, יָכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 7's reading of the פסוק for a new case where the afternoon half is ruined.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lost or impure afternoon half is replaced with half of a new complete עשרון, not with a separate half-עשרון.

steps.title: How the replacement for a lost half works
steps.stepSummary: When the afternoon half is lost or becomes טמא, the כהן גדול brings a new whole עשרון, divides it, and offers only half. In the end, two halves are offered and two are lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? He brings a whole עשרון from his house, divides it, offers half, and the other half is lost. So two halves are offered and two halves are lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains exactly how to follow the rule from Step 8, that a lost afternoon half must be replaced by a half taken from a whole עשרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he may not bring a lone half from home, he must bring a full new עשרון and use only half of it. The other half of the new עשרון goes unused. Together with the half that was lost, that makes two lost halves, while the morning half and the new half are offered.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, the measure of flour for this offering
From his house, meaning from his own private funds
And he divides it in half
Is lost, meaning it is not offered

phrases.english: How so?
He brings a whole tenth [from his house],
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets belongs to the corrected wording. Some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: and divides it, and offers half,
and the other half is lost.
It turns out that two halves are offered,
phrases.notes: The morning half and the half from the new עשרון are the two that get offered.

phrases.english: and two halves are lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how to carry out the rule from Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A lost afternoon half is replaced by half of a new whole עשרון, so two halves are offered and two are lost.

steps.title: The כהן גדול dies after the morning half
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a new case. The כהן גדול offered the morning half and died. Maybe the new כהן גדול brings just half an עשרון from home, or uses the first one's leftover half?
steps.simpleTranslation: If a כהן גדול offered half in the morning and died, and another was appointed in his place, you might think the new one brings half an עשרון from his house, or offers the leftover half of the first one's עשרון.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets up two possible wrong ideas about what the new כהן גדול should bring. This prepares the way for the פסוק to answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two easy options are suggested. He could bring only the half he needs, or he could finish the first כהן גדול's עשרון. Both would avoid waste, which is why the ברייתא needs a פסוק to reject them.

keyTerms.meaning: And they appointed another in his place
One might have thought, the opening of a mistaken first idea

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁהִקְרִיב מֶחֱצָה שַׁחֲרִית וָמֵת,
phrases.english: A High Priest who offered half in the morning and died,
and they appointed another in his place,
one might think he should bring half a tenth from his house,
or the half of the first one's tenth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a lost half to the case of the כהן גדול's death, and gives the source for the ruling stated in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up two mistaken options for the new כהן גדול: a half from home, or the first one's leftover half.

steps.title: The פסוק requires a half from a whole
steps.stepSummary: The words 'ומחציתה בערב' teach that the new כהן גדול must bring and offer half of a complete עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And half of it in the evening.' This means he brings and offers a half taken from a whole עשרון.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from Step 10 with the פסוק. Both easy options are rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Half of it' means half of a whole עשרון that belongs to this offering. So a lone half brought from home does not count. The first כהן גדול's leftover also does not work, because the new כהן גדול must bring his own whole עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches, introducing the source that settles the question
And half of it in the evening

phrases.english: The verse states: "And half of it in the evening" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:13

phrases.english: he brings and offers half of a whole one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects both options raised in Step 10, using the same word that was explained in Step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The new כהן גדול must offer half of a complete עשרון.

steps.title: How the new כהן גדול carries this out
steps.stepSummary: The new כהן גדול brings a whole עשרון, divides it, offers half, and the other half is lost. So two halves are lost and two are offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? He brings a whole עשרון, divides it, and offers half, and the other half is lost. So two halves are lost and two halves are offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out the practical steps for the new כהן גדול, using the same pattern as Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first כהן גדול's afternoon half is never offered, and half of the new עשרון is also left over. That gives two lost halves. The first one's morning half and the new one's afternoon half are the two that get offered.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out, the final result

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a half is lost or the כהן גדול dies, the rule is the same. A whole עשרון must be brought and divided, so two halves are offered and two are lost.

phrases.english: How so?
He brings a whole tenth and divides it,
and he offers half, and the other half is lost.
It turns out that two halves are lost,
phrases.notes: One half from each כהן גדול goes unused.

phrases.english: and two halves are offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the rule from Step 11 is carried out in practice.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: After the כהן גדול's death, the new one divides a fresh whole עשרון, so two halves are offered and two are lost.

steps.title: What to do with the two leftover halves
steps.stepSummary: A תנא taught before רב נחמן that the first כהן גדול's leftover half and the second's leftover half are left until they become unfit, and are then burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב נחמן: the first half and the second half are left until their form is spoiled, and then they go out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching answers a question left open by the earlier steps: what happens to the two 'lost' halves?
steps.deeperAnalysis: These halves are holy flour that was never offered, so they are not simply thrown out. They are left overnight until they become unfit, and then they are burned in the place set aside for burning.

keyTerms.meaning: A scholar whose job was to recite ברייתות
Their form should be spoiled, meaning they are left overnight until they become unfit
The place set aside for burning holy things that became unfit

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Naḥman:
The first half and the second half –
phrases.notes: He means the leftover half of each כהן גדול's עשרון, the two 'lost' halves from Step 12.

phrases.english: their form should be spoiled,
phrases.notes: They are left overnight until they become unfit.

phrases.english: and they go out to the place of burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what is done with the 'lost' halves described in Steps 9 and 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leftover halves are left until they become unfit and then burned.

steps.title: Why should the second half have to wait before burning?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן accepts that the first כהן גדול's leftover half needs עיבור צורה. He questions why the second's leftover half needs it, since it was meant to be lost from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: I understand the first half, which was fit to be offered. But why does the second half need to be left until it spoils? From the beginning it was brought only to be lost.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges the ברייתא from Step 13. He questions the rule that the second כהן גדול's leftover half must be left overnight before being burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that was once fit for the מזבח must be left until it becomes unfit, and only then burned. The first כהן גדול's half was fit at first, so waiting makes sense. The second כהן גדול's extra half was known from the start to be a loss, so it seems it was never really fit and could be burned right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Letting something's form spoil (left overnight) before it is burned
It comes to be lost, set aside for destruction

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
phrases.notes: He is speaking to the תנא who just taught the ברייתא in Step 13.

phrases.english: Granted, the first was fit for offering,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֵׁנִי לְמָה לֵיהּ עִיבּוּר צוּרָה?
phrases.english: but the second, why does it need its form to spoil?
From the outset it came to be lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רִאשׁוֹן אִיחֲזִי לְהַקְרָבָה, אֶלָּא שֵׁנִי לְמָה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling taught in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that the second כהן גדול's leftover half needs עיבור צורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עיבור צורה applies only to something that was once fit. The second half was set aside to be lost from the start, so it was never fit.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows the school of רבה בר אבוה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that the ברייתא follows the תנא of רבה בר אבוה's school. That תנא holds that even פיגול needs עיבור צורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who said this to you? It is the תנא of the school of רבה בר אבוה, who says that even פיגול needs its form to spoil.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers his own question. The ברייתא comes from a תנא who requires the waiting period for every unfit offering, even פיגול, which is unfit by תורה law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול is unfit by תורה law, yet this תנא still requires עיבור צורה before burning it. If even פיגול needs it, then the second half, which was never meant to be offered, also needs it. So the ruling is correct, but only according to this one opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Whose opinion is this?
A קרבן made unfit by a wrong intention about its time of eating or burning

phrases.english: The one who said this to you, who is he?

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ הוּא,
phrases.english: It is the תנא of the school of Rabba bar Avuh,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ פִּיגּוּל טָעוּן עִיבּוּר צוּרָה.
phrases.english: who says: even piggul requires its form to spoil.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲמַר לָךְ, מַנִּי? תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves Step 14 by naming the opinion behind the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ברייתא to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Something meant to be lost from the start needs no עיבור צורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to the school of רבה בר אבוה, every unfit offering needs עיבור צורה, even פיגול, which is unfit by תורה law. So the second half needs it too.

steps.title: רב אשי: both halves were fit when divided
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ברייתא can follow even the רבנן. When the כהן divided the עשרון, he could choose either half to offer, so both halves were fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: You can even say it follows the רבנן. At the time he divides them, he can offer whichever half he wants, so both halves are fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer. Under his answer, the ברייתא does not have to follow a minority opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי rejects the idea that the second half was "lost from the start." At the moment of dividing, no particular half had been chosen for loss, so each half was fit to be offered. Because each half was once fit, even the רבנן agree it needs עיבור צורה.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the רבנן (the majority view)

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain why the second half needs עיבור צורה. One says the ברייתא follows רבה בר אבוה's school, where even פיגול needs it. רב אשי says both halves were fit at the moment of dividing.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You can even say it follows the Rabbis,
since at the time that he divides them,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, meaning "that he divides them."

phrases.english: if he wants, he offers this one,
and if he wants, he offers that one,
they are indeed fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to Step 14 that works even according to the רבנן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the status of the second half
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second half was set aside to be lost from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the כהן divides the עשרון, either half could be offered, so both were fit and both need עיבור צורה.

steps.title: How are the חביתין prepared?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic: the method for preparing the כהן גדול's חביתין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: The חביתין of the כהן גדול, how are they made?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question about how the חביתין are actually cooked. This line sets up the dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic shifts from what happens to leftover halves to how the offering is prepared. The question is about the order of steps in cooking it.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily griddle-cake מנחה of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: It was stated: The griddle-cakes of the High Priest,
how are they made?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: חֲבִיתֵּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, כֵּיצַד עוֹשִׂין אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic about the same offering
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct order of baking and frying the חביתין

steps.title: Bake then fry, or fry then bake
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says to bake it and then fry it. רבי חנינא says to fry it and then bake it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: He bakes it and afterward fries it. רבי אסי said in the name of רבי חנינא: He fries it and afterward bakes it.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question with opposite orders. One says to bake first, and the other says to fry first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the חביתין is both baked and fried. They argue only about which comes first.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
He bakes it, and afterward he fries it.
Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
He fries it, and afterward he bakes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אוֹפָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְטַגְּנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 17 with a dispute
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: bake, then fry. רבי חנינא: fry, then bake.

steps.title: Support for baking first: the loaves must be baked while still nice
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reads ״תֻּפִינֵי״ as ״תֹּאפֶינָּה נָאָה״, bake it while it is still nice. That supports baking first and frying afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: My view makes sense. ״תֻּפִינֵי״ means 'bake it while it is beautiful.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא brings a proof from the פסוק for one side of the argument in Step 18. He supports the order 'bake, then fry.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: He splits the word ״תֻּפִינֵי״ into two words: תֹּאפֶינָּה (bake it) + נָאָה (beautiful). If the baking has to happen while the dough is still fresh and nice, then the baking comes first, before any frying. That matches רבי יוחנן's order.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense according to my view
A word in the פסוק about the חביתין (ויקרא 6:14), read here as a hint to how they are baked
Bake it while it is beautiful (still fresh and untouched)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said:
It makes sense according to my view,
phrases.notes: He means the view he holds in the argument from the last step, which is bake first and then fry.

phrases.english: "Tufinei" means: bake it while it is beautiful.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:14. He reads the one word as two: 'bake it' + 'beautiful.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof from the פסוק for the 'bake then fry' side of Step 18.

steps.title: Support for frying first: the loaves are baked once they are partly cooked
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי reads ״תֻּפִינֵי״ as ״תֹּאפֶינָּה נָא״, bake it when it is already partly cooked. That supports frying first and baking afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: My view makes sense. ״תֻּפִינֵי״ means 'bake it when it is partly cooked.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי brings his own reading of the same word to support the other side. He supports 'fry, then bake.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the second half of the word as נָא, partly cooked, instead of נָאָה, beautiful. If the dough is already partly cooked when it goes in to bake, it must have been fried first. That matches רבי חנינא's order.

keyTerms.meaning: Bake it when it is partly cooked (half-done)

steps.confusionAlert: נָא and נָאָה look almost the same, but they mean opposite stages. נָאָה (beautiful) means the baking comes first. נָא (partly cooked) means the frying comes first.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר: כְּוָותֵיהּ דִּידִי מִסְתַּבְּרָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said: It makes sense according to my view,
"Tufinei" means: bake it when it is partly cooked.
phrases.notes: Partly cooked from the frying, so in his reading the frying comes before the baking.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר: כְּוָותֵיהּ דִּידִי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the same word to support the 'fry then bake' side.

steps.title: The same argument already appears among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the אמוראים' argument matches an earlier argument in a ברייתא. The תנא קמא reads ״תֹּאפֶינָּה נָא״ and רבי reads ״תֹּאפֶינָּה נָאָה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like an argument between תנאים: ״תֻּפִינֵי״ means 'bake it when partly cooked.' רבי says: 'bake it while beautiful.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that this exact argument was already held by תנאים in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא has רבי אסי's reading (fry first). רבי has רבי חייא בר אבא's reading (bake first). So each אמורא has a תנא who agrees with him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like an argument between תנאים
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: It is like an argument between תנאים: "Tufinei" means bake it when it is partly cooked.
Rebbi says: bake it while it is beautiful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the two אמוראים' readings to an earlier argument between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא reads נָא (fry first), and רבי reads נָאָה (bake first).

steps.title: רבי יוסי: bake it a lot, so both readings are true
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reads ״תֹּאפֶינָּה רַבָּה″, bake it many times. The גמרא explains that he accepts both נָא and נָאָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: bake it a lot. He holds the 'partly cooked' reading and he also holds the 'beautiful' reading.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a third view that combines the first two. The גמרא then explains what he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״תֻּפִינֵי״ is plural, so רבי יוסי says the baking happens more than once. First it is baked while still beautiful (נָאָה). Then it is fried. Then it is baked again once it is partly cooked (נָא).

keyTerms.meaning: Bake it a lot (more than once)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three orders: bake then fry (נָאָה), fry then bake (נָא), and רבי יוסי's bake, fry, bake again (both).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: bake it a lot.
phrases.notes: He learns this from the word ״תֻּפִינֵי״ being plural. 'A lot' means more than one baking.

phrases.aramaic: אִית לֵיהּ נָא, וְאִית לֵיהּ נָאָה.
phrases.english: He holds 'partly cooked,' and he holds 'beautiful.'
phrases.notes: This line is the גמרא explaining רבי יוסי: bake first, fry, then bake again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third תנא who combines both readings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חביתין are baked, fried, and baked again.

steps.title: משנה: the חביתין are prepared inside the עזרה and override שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere: the kneading, shaping and baking of the חביתין happen inside the עזרה and override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: the כהן גדול's חביתין are kneaded, shaped and baked inside, and this overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה. It is setting up a question about where this rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says two things: all the preparation is done 'inside,' in the עזרה, and it is done even on שבת. The next step asks for the source of the שבת rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside the עזרה (the בית המקדש courtyard)
They override שבת (they may be done on שבת)

phrases.english: We learned there: the כהן גדול's griddle-cakes —
phrases.notes: The משנה is in מנחות 96a.

phrases.english: their kneading, their shaping, and their baking are done inside,
and they override שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the order of preparation to a new question: preparing the חביתין on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The kneading, shaping and baking of the חביתין are done in the עזרה and override שבת.

steps.title: Where do we learn that this overrides שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that preparing the חביתין overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that the חביתין are prepared even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally kneading and baking are forbidden on שבת. One could think the חביתין should simply be baked on Friday, so the גמרא wants to know why this work has to be done on שבת itself.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where do we know these things?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that preparing the חביתין overrides שבת

steps.title: רב הונא: the loaves must be fresh, so they cannot be baked the day before
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reads ״תֻּפִינֵי״ as ״תֹּאפֶינָּה נָאָה״: the loaves must be nice when offered. If they were baked on Friday they would spoil, so they must be made on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: ״תֻּפִינֵי״ means 'bake it so it is beautiful.' If you baked it yesterday, it would swell up and spoil.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question from Step 24 using the same word ״תֻּפִינֵי״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here נָאָה means the loaf must be fresh and nice when it is offered. A loaf baked on Friday would be spoiled by שבת, so the baking has to happen on שבת itself. That is why it overrides שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: Earlier, נָאָה was used to decide the order of baking and frying. רב הונא uses the same word for something else: the loaf must be fresh when it is offered.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
"Tufinei" means: bake it so it is beautiful,
and if one baked it from yesterday,
phrases.notes: 'Yesterday' here means Friday, the day before שבת.

phrases.english: it would swell up and spoil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The loaves must be fresh and nice. Baking them on Friday would spoil them, so they must be baked on שבת.

steps.title: רב יוסף: just keep it fresh by covering it with greens
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רב הונא: the loaf could be baked on Friday and kept fresh under greens, so freshness does not prove it must be baked on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: Say that one covers it with greens!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב הונא's source from Step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's whole reason was that a loaf baked on Friday would spoil. רב יוסף says there is an easy fix: cover it with greens to keep it fresh. If so, the need for freshness does not force anyone to bake on שבת, and רב הונא's proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it (raises a strong objection)
Covers it / presses it under, to keep it fresh

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects to this:
Say that one covers it with greens!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's proof that the חביתין must be baked on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Freshness can be kept by covering the loaf with greens, so baking on שבת is not needed to keep it nice.

steps.title: School of רבי ישמעאל: 'It shall be made', even on שבת and in טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns from the word ״תֵּעָשֶׂה″ that the חביתין must be made under all conditions, even on שבת and even in a state of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'It shall be made' means even on שבת. 'It shall be made' also means even in טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source for why baking the חביתין overrides שבת. This one does not depend on keeping the loaves fresh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's proof from ״נָאָה״ (nice and fresh) was knocked down, because a Friday loaf could stay fresh. The school of רבי ישמעאל reads the word ״תֵּעָשֶׂה״ as a command to make the loaves no matter what. So nothing stops it: not שבת and not טומאה. The rule now comes straight from the wording of the פסוק, not from a practical worry about freshness.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It shall be made', the word in the פסוק about the חביתין

steps.whyThisMatters: This source avoids רב יוסף's challenge completely. It does not depend on freshness at all, only on the extra meaning in the word ״תֵּעָשֶׂה״.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"It shall be made": even on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:14

phrases.english: "It shall be made": even in a state of ritual impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יוסף's challenge weakened רב הונא's freshness proof, this gives a different source that does not rely on freshness.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that preparing the חביתין overrides שבת (asked in step 24).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״תֵּעָשֶׂה״ teaches that the חביתין are made in every situation, even on שבת and even in טומאה.

steps.title: אביי begins a different source from 'perpetually'
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens another explanation by quoting the פסוק ״סֹלֶת מִנְחָה תָּמִיד״. His point about the word ״תָּמִיד״ continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says, 'Fine flour for a meal offering perpetually'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts giving his own source for why the חביתין override שבת. Here he only quotes the פסוק, so he is setting up his explanation, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי points to a different word, ״תָּמִיד״ (perpetually, always). The word that will matter is ״תָּמִיד״, which suggests the offering happens every single day without a break. His explanation of how he uses it continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Abaye said: The verse states:
"Fine flour for a meal offering perpetually"
